(CNN) -- Venus Williams is most often seen wiping perspiration from her brow as she thunders around the court contesting championship tennis matches. Venus Williams steps off the tennis court and into the pool in a series of photos to be featured in Italian Marie Claire. These photos show the world number six in a more reflective mood, posing for a 16-page fashion spread in the Italian edition of Marie Claire. They were taken in Miami, Florida in December last year by her friend and photographer Koto Bolofo. "I love working with Koto," Venus told CNN in an interview for "Revealed." "I think he's my biggest fan and he believes in me, I'm not sure why, but he does so I've got to accept that," she laughed. They planned to shoot 20 outfits in one day, a hectic schedule that included one photo that had been two years in the making.  See video of the photo shoot » . "I've got it pictured in my mind that she's going to be playing tennis underwater," Bolofo told CNN. When the sun finally emerged from behind a cloud, Bolofo ordered Venus into her bathers. "I'm excited it's my first underwater tennis venture, so I feel a little nervous, but I think I'll come through," Venus said. "I want her smiling and making it look as if it's natural and it's not an effort," Bolofo explained. "It's going to be whimsical and fun. That's the fun part of the shoot." Fashion is an important part of Venus Williams' life. She has her own clothing company, EleVen, which produces tennis outfits and casual clothing. She sketches ideas, but says she's not the chief designer, by any stretch. "There are other people designing stuff. I couldn't do it on my own," she said, adding, "I don't do technical drawing, I hated it in school. I refuse to do this on the computer. I'd rather just do it by hand." Venus' status in the ranks of the world's top tennis players gives her a unique position to be able to market her products and she often wears them on court. Then there's her interior design company; Venus launched V Starr Interiors while still in her early twenties. Despite her public business interests, Venus told CNN she's not interested in seizing the spotlight for any reason other than as one of the world's best tennis players. "Fame has never been important to me. My goals have always been to excel in tennis, and to win championships. Fame has never been my focus and I don't really try to grow it at all," she said. Venus' relaxed attitude has earned her respect beyond the world of tennis. Hip hop star Wyclef Jean released a song in her honor last year called "I'm Ready."  Listen to the song » . "[It's like] when a painter is inspired," Jean told CNN. "When I'm inspired by an individual I just write a song about them ... I said her name is Venus, ruler of the universe." Venus was thrilled. "I've got it on my computer, all the different instrumentals, the different versions, the different cuts. I love it," she told CNN. Venus Williams is back on court this week at the Barclays Dubai Tennis Championships. Naturally, she's hoping to win after a disappointing early exit from the Australian Open in January. While tennis remains her prime obsession, Venus told CNN it's not the most important thing in her life. "I would say definitely the most important thing in my life is growing spiritually. And doing what God requires of me -- that's always a learning experience day in and day out," she said. Watch Venus Williams on Revealed this week at the times below: . ALL TIMES GMT Wednesday, February 18: 0930, 1830 Saturday, February 21: 0830, 1900 Sunday, February 22: 0530, 1830 Monday, February 23: 0400 .

(CNN) — Tennis fans are accustomed to seeing Venus Williams racing powerfully across the court and brushing sweat from her forehead during championship matches. But for a 16-page fashion feature in the Italian edition of *Marie Claire*, the world No. 6 traded the court for a swimming pool and revealed a quieter, more contemplative side.

The photographs were shot in Miami, Florida, in December of the previous year by Williams’ friend, photographer Koto Bolofo.

Williams spoke about the collaboration during an interview for CNN’s *Revealed*. “I love working with Koto,” she said. Laughing, she added that he might be her greatest admirer because he believes in her—although she does not know why—and that she simply has to accept it.

The pair intended to photograph 20 outfits in a single day. Their demanding timetable also included an image Bolofo had been imagining for two years. **See video of the photo shoot »**

Bolofo told CNN that he envisioned Williams playing tennis beneath the water. Once the sun finally broke through the clouds, he instructed her to put on her swimwear.

Williams said she was excited because it was her first attempt at underwater tennis. Although she admitted to feeling somewhat anxious, she was confident she would succeed.

Bolofo wanted Williams to smile and make the difficult scene appear effortless and natural. He described the concept as playful, fanciful and the most enjoyable element of the shoot.

Fashion occupies a significant place in Williams’ life. She owns EleVen, a clothing business that makes both tennis apparel and casual wear. While she draws sketches of her ideas, she emphasized that she is far from being the company’s principal designer.

Williams explained that other people also create the clothes and that she could not manage the work by herself. She does not produce technical drawings because she disliked doing them at school, and she refuses to design on a computer, preferring to work by hand.

As one of the highest-ranked tennis players in the world, Williams is in the unusual position of being able to promote her own products, often wearing EleVen clothing during matches.

She also owns an interior-design firm. Williams founded V Starr Interiors when she was still in her early twenties.

Despite her publicly visible business activities, Williams told CNN that she has no desire to attract attention for anything except her achievements as one of the world’s leading tennis players. She said celebrity has never mattered to her; her ambitions have always centered on performing at the highest level in tennis and winning championships. She has never pursued fame or made an effort to increase it.

Her easygoing outlook has won admiration outside tennis as well. The previous year, hip-hop artist Wyclef Jean honored her with a song titled “I’m Ready.” **Listen to the song »**

Jean compared the creative impulse to the inspiration experienced by a painter. He told CNN that when a person inspires him, he writes a song about that individual. In the lyrics, he called her Venus, “ruler of the universe.”

Williams was delighted by the tribute. She told CNN that she keeps all the instrumentals, alternate versions and different edits on her computer and loves them.

This week, Williams returns to competition at the Barclays Dubai Tennis Championships. After being eliminated earlier than expected from the Australian Open in January, she is, naturally, aiming for victory.

Although tennis remains her foremost passion, Williams said it is not the central priority in her life. She identified spiritual growth—and fulfilling what God asks of her—as most important, describing it as an ongoing learning process that continues every day.

# Venus Williams makes a splash in underwater fashion shoot

**By CNN Style**

Venus Williams has faced booming serves, marathon rallies and the pressure of championship point. For an Italian *Marie Claire* fashion shoot, however, the tennis star confronted a different challenge: playing her sport underwater.

Photographed by Koto Bolofo, Williams traded the familiar intensity of the court for the dreamlike stillness of a swimming pool. Submerged in flowing designer clothes and accompanied by a tennis racket, she appears less like an athlete in competition than a modern mermaid suspended between sport and high fashion.

“Underwater, everything slows down,” Williams said of the experience. “You have to stay calm, hold your breath and trust what you’re doing.”

Bolofo said the shoot was intended to show a side of Williams that spectators rarely see during a match. “Venus has this extraordinary combination of power and grace,” he said. “In the water, her movements became almost like a ballet.”

The images reflect a long-standing interest in style for Williams, whose ambitions extend well beyond tennis. She is the founder of the fashion label EleVen, which brings bright colors and runway-inspired details to athletic clothing. She also runs V Starr, an interior design company that has worked on residential, hospitality and commercial projects.

For Williams, those ventures are not merely celebrity sidelines. She studied fashion design and has spoken frequently about the discipline required to build a business while maintaining an elite sporting career.

“I love tennis, but I also love creating,” she said. “Fashion and design give me another way to express myself.”

Her ability to move between sport, music and fashion has attracted admirers including musician Wyclef Jean, who has described Williams as both an athlete and an inspiration. “Venus is a champion, but she’s also an artist,” Jean said. “She has style, strength and soul.”

Despite global recognition, Williams has said fame itself has never been her central motivation. Winning, improving and pursuing work she believes in matter more, she said, than being treated as a celebrity.

“Fame is not the goal,” Williams said. “You have to know who you are when the cheering stops.”

That perspective is closely tied to her spirituality. Raised as a Jehovah’s Witness, Williams has credited faith with helping her remain grounded through victories, defeats and intense public scrutiny. Her beliefs, she has said, offer a sense of proportion in a profession where rankings and results can easily become all-consuming.

“Spirituality keeps life in perspective,” she said. “Tennis is important to me, but it isn’t everything.”

The underwater photographs may present Williams in a serene, otherworldly setting, but her competitive focus remains firmly on the court. She is preparing for her next tournament in Dubai, where another strong international field — and another chance to add to her list of titles — awaits.

For now, the *Marie Claire* shoot captures the many identities Williams has assembled over her career: champion, entrepreneur, designer and fashion figure. Even beneath the surface, racket in hand, she remains unmistakably Venus.

Yet tennis remained central as Williams prepared to return to competition at the Barclays Dubai Tennis Championships. That balance—faith, family, tennis and enterprise—helps explain why an underwater photo session can feel like more than a novelty.
